question: What is the main sterol found in the cell membrane of fungi?
explanation: Spot on! Fungal cell membranes use ergosterol. This is super helpful in pharmacology because many antifungal drugs target ergosterol, leaving our human cells (which use cholesterol) alone. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h1)

question: Why are fungal infections sometimes trickier to treat than bacterial infections?

options.A: Antifungal drugs cannot dissolve in human blood
options.B: Fungi multiply much faster than bacterial cells
options.C: Bacterial cell walls are made of strong chitin
options.D: Fungi share a close cellular structure with human cells

explanation: You got it! Because both fungi and human cells are eukaryotes, it's harder to find drugs that kill the fungus without harming our own cells. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h1)

question: How do echinocandins fight against fungal infections?

options.B: By blocking beta-D-glucan synthesis in the cell wall
options.C: By binding directly to ergosterol to form pores

explanation: Brilliant! Echinocandins attack the fungal cell wall by blocking beta-D-glucan. Without this support, the cell becomes unstable and bursts. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h2)

question: What is the main way azole antifungal drugs work?

options.A: Creating physical holes in the outer cell membrane
options.B: Preventing the conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol
options.C: Destroying the chitin layer of suppuration
options.D: Preventing the uptake of vital glucose molecules

explanation: Well done! Azoles block a key enzyme needed to make ergosterol. Without enough ergosterol, the fungal cell membrane weakens and fails. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h2)

question: Which powerful antifungal drug is famous for causing severe kidney issues and shaking chills during an IV infusion?
explanation: That's right! Nurses often call it 'Amphotericin B' (or 'Ampho-terrible' in clinical ward gist) because it saves lives from severe fungal infections, but it's tough on the kidneys and makes patients shake. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h3)

question: A patient is leaving the hospital after treatment for a deep fungal infection. Which oral azole is commonly used for long-term follow-up care?
explanation: Correct! Fluconazole is great for outpatient step-down therapy because it absorbs very well by mouth and reaches tissues all over the body. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h3)

question: Why can nystatin oral liquid be used safely for mouth thrush without causing major body-wide side effects?

options.A: It is completely neutralized by normal saliva enzymes
options.B: It is poorly absorbed from the digestive tract into the blood
options.C: It breaks down instantly upon touching the oral mucosa
options.D: It only targets bacterial cell walls instead of human cells

explanation: Spot on! Nystatin stays right where it is needed in the mouth or gut. Because very little enters the bloodstream, whole-body side effects are rare. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h4)

question: Why do fungal infections of the toenails (onychomycosis) usually need oral pills instead of just a surface cream?

options.A: Topical creams cannot penetrate deeply enough through the hard nail plate
options.B: Fungi living in toenails are completely immune to all topical antifungal creams
options.C: Topical medications wash away too quickly from the foot due to sweat
options.D: Nail infections are always caused by systemic internal organ failure

explanation: Correct! The nail plate is thick and tough, acting like a shield that surface creams can't pass through. Pills are needed to reach the fungus from within. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h4)

question: What weather condition in tropical regions like Nigeria contributes greatly to skin fungal infections?

options.A: Frequent consumption of contaminated municipal water supplies
options.B: High environmental humidity and warm weather conditions
options.C: Lack of personal hygiene products in local markets
options.D: Widespread resistance to standard antibacterial vaccines

explanation: You got it! Fungi love warmth and moisture. Our wonderful tropical climate means we see plenty of superficial skin fungal infections in clinical practice. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h5)

question: Which fungal infection is a major cause of meningitis in patients with advanced HIV/AIDS seen in Nigerian hospitals?
explanation: Correct! Cryptococcal meningitis is a serious opportunistic infection in immunocompromised patients, and spotting it early saves lives on the wards. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h5)

question: Which body organ must a nurse monitor closely when a patient is on long-term azole antifungal therapy?
explanation: Well done! Azole drugs can stress the liver, so checking liver enzyme blood tests regularly is a key part of safe nursing care. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h6)

question: Why is it dangerous to combine certain azoles with blood thinners like warfarin?

options.A: Warfarin destroys the chemical structure of azoles in the bloodstream
options.B: Both drugs together instantly destroy the red blood cell count
options.C: Azoles block warfarin from entering the kidneys for excretion
options.D: Azoles inhibit liver enzymes, causing warfarin levels to rise dangerously

explanation: Spot on! Azoles slow down the liver enzymes that break down warfarin. This causes warfarin to build up in the blood, vastly increasing bleeding risks. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h6)

question: What is the most important advice a nurse should give a patient taking a multi-week course of antifungal drugs?

options.A: Double the next dose whenever a single daily dose is accidentally missed
options.B: Take the pills only on days when itching or burning becomes severe
options.C: Complete the entire prescribed course even if symptoms disappear early
options.D: Stop the medication immediately if mild skin dryness or nausea occurs

explanation: You nailed it! Stopping early is the number one reason fungal infections bounce right back. Always encourage patients to finish the full dose. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h7)

question: How should a nurse instruct a patient to use nystatin oral suspension for mouth thrush?

options.A: Swallow the liquid immediately on an empty stomach with a full glass of water
options.B: Swish the liquid thoroughly around the mouth before swallowing it
options.C: Dilute the entire bottle in a glass of cold fruit juice and drink it fast
options.D: Gargle the liquid at the back of the throat and spit it out without swallowing

explanation: Correct! The medication needs time to touch all the infected spots in the mouth before it is swallowed down to coat the throat or gut. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h7)
